dc31.title: Notifications dropdown
dc31.summary: A project-management app header. Make the bell show an unread badge and open a notifications dropdown that marks items read.
dc31.brief:
The header of Tasklane, a project board. AppHeader has the nav, search, a BellButton that does nothing yet, and the user's Avatar. The board below is static.

Read api.ts: getNotifications() (0.4–1s), markRead(id) and markAllRead() (0.3–0.7s each). Also read utils/time.ts (timeAgo, isToday, a fixed NOW) and components/ (Avatar, BellIcon). Reuse them.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~16 min): Today / Earlier groups.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–15 Core · 15–20 Next + change · 20–25 polish and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The badge needs the unread count before the menu is ever opened, so I load notifications on mount, not on open. I'll make one NotificationsMenu component that owns items, loading and open, and replaces BellButton. Unread count is derived with filter, never stored. Clicking an item updates it locally first and calls markRead in the background (optimistic). For click-outside I put a ref on the wrapper (bell + menu) and listen for mousedown on document only while open, removing the listener in the cleanup."
requirements: After getNotifications() resolves, the bell shows a red badge with the unread count (4). The badge is not rendered when the count is 0

Clicking the bell toggles a 360px dropdown (title "Notifications") listing each notification: Avatar, actor + text, and timeAgo ("18m ago"). Unread rows have a tinted background and a blue dot. While still loading it says "Loading notifications…"
Clicking an unread notification marks it read immediately (dot and tint go, badge decrements) and calls markRead(id)
Mark all as read in the dropdown header marks every item read, removes the badge and calls markAllRead(). It is disabled when nothing is unread
Clicking anywhere outside the bell + dropdown closes it, and so does Escape. Clicking inside the dropdown does not close it

change.title: Today / Earlier
change.html:
"The list is one long wall. Split it by day."

  • Group the notifications under two small uppercase headings: Today and Earlier (use isToday(createdAt) from utils/time.ts).
  • A group with no items shows no heading. Order within each group stays newest first.

Hint: two derived arrays, and a small NotificationGroup component that returns null when empty.

hints: State placement: one component owns items, loading and open. The badge, the list and "Mark all" all read the same items.
Derived: const unreadCount = items.filter((n) => { return !n.read; }).length; Then let badge = null; if (unreadCount > 0) { badge = ...; }
Marking one read without mutating: setItems((prev) => { return prev.map((n) => { if (n.id === id) { return { ...n, read: true }; } return n; }); }); then call markRead(id).
Click outside: search mdn Node.contains and react click outside ref. Put useRef on the wrapper that contains both the bell and the menu, otherwise clicking the bell closes and reopens it.

The effect shape: useEffect(() => { if (!open) { return; } function handle(e: MouseEvent) { if (ref.current && !ref.current.contains(e.target as Node)) { setOpen(false); } } document.addEventListener("mousedown", handle); return () => { document.removeEventListener("mousedown", handle); }; }, [open]);
rubric: Loaded on mount so the badge is right before opening
Unread count derived, not a second piece of state
Optimistic read update with map + spread (no mutation)
Document listeners added only while open and removed in cleanup
Ref on the wrapper so the bell click doesn't fight the outside click
Reused Avatar, BellIcon, timeAgo and isToday
Grouping done with derived arrays; empty group hidden

dc32.title: Onboarding wizard
dc32.summary: A fitness app sign-up. Turn the single Profile form into a 3-step wizard with validation, a step indicator and a final submit.
dc32.brief:
The sign-up screen of Stride. OnboardingWizard already holds the whole form in one form object and renders ProfileStep. The Continue button does nothing.

Read components/Steps.tsx: ProfileStep and PreferencesStep are done and take values, errors and onChange. Field already shows an error in red if you pass one. utils/validate.ts has isValidEmail and isIntInRange. createAccount(data) in api.ts takes 0.7–1.3s.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~19 min): jump back from the indicator.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–19 Core · 19–26 change · 26–30 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The form object already lives in the wizard, so going Back keeps the values for free as long as I don't unmount the state. I add step (0, 1, 2) and errors. A pure validateStep(step, form) returns an errors object; Continue only advances when it's empty. The body is an if/else on step. Submit sets submitting, calls createAccount, and when it resolves I store the account and render a success screen instead of the wizard. The indicator is a small component that gets current."
requirements: Three steps: Profile → Preferences (uses PreferencesStep) → Review. Continue moves forward, Back (hidden on step 1) moves back, and values typed earlier are still there

Continue validates the current step first. Profile: name required ("Enter your name"), valid email ("Enter a valid email"), age 13–99 ("Age must be between 13 and 99"). Preferences: a goal ("Pick a goal"). Errors show under the fields and the step does not change

Review lists Name, Email, Age, Goal (label, not id), Workouts ("3 days a week") and Units. Create my plan calls createAccount(form), shows "Creating…" and is disabled while waiting, then shows "You're all set, {name}!" with the returned plan name
A step indicator above the title: three labelled steps, current one highlighted, completed ones show ✓. The eyebrow reads "Step 2 of 3"
Fixing a field clears its error right away (no need to press Continue again to see it go)

change.title: Jump back from the indicator
change.html:
"On Review people want to fix their email without pressing Back twice."

  • Completed steps in the indicator are clickable and jump straight to that step (values kept).
  • The current step and future steps are not clickable (you can't skip validation by jumping forward).

hints: New state next to form: const [step, setStep] = useState(0); and const [errors, setErrors] = useState<StepErrors>({});
Write validation as a plain function outside the component: function validateStep(step: number, form: OnboardingData): StepErrors. It's easy to test and the component stays short.
"Is the errors object empty?" Search: mdn Object.keys. if (Object.keys(found).length > 0) { setErrors(found); return; }
Pick the body above the return: let body; if (step === 0) { body = <ProfileStep ... />; } else if (step === 1) { ... } else { body = <ReviewStep values={form} />; }
Change: render each indicator step as a <button disabled={i >= current}> and call onJump(i). Disabled buttons ignore clicks, so the guard is in the markup.
rubric: Single form object kept in the wizard (Back keeps values)
Validation is a pure function, run on Continue
Errors passed to the existing Field via the step components
Submit shows a pending state and can't double-submit
Success screen driven by the API result
Indicator derived from step; forward jumps impossible
Reused isValidEmail / isIntInRange / GOALS

dc33.title: Poll with live results
dc33.summary: A gaming-community post with a poll. Vote optimistically, animate result bars with percentages, and allow changing your vote.
dc33.brief:
A post in Guildhall, a dark-themed gaming community. PollWidget already loads the poll with getPoll() and renders the four options as buttons that do nothing.

Read api.ts: vote(optionId) takes 0.6–1.2s and returns the whole updated Poll (it moves your vote if you already voted). utils/poll.ts has percent and formatVotes.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~16 min): Change vote.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–15 Core · 15–21 change · 21–25 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"poll stays the single source of truth; myVote is in it. Results show when myVote !== null. On click I update poll locally first (+1 on the chosen option, set myVote) so the bars move instantly, then call vote and replace poll with the server's copy. Total and percentages are derived. For the animation I render the bar span always, with width 0% before voting, and CSS transition: width does the rest."
requirements: Clicking an option votes for it immediately (optimistic): the options switch to results without waiting for the API, and vote(optionId) is called. When it resolves, the poll is replaced with the server's data

Results: each option shows a filled bar behind the label whose width is its percentage, and the percentage on the right ("10%"). Under the list: "101 votes · Closes in 2 days". Your option has a ✓ and a stronger gradient bar
After voting, the options are disabled: you cannot vote twice
Bars animate from 0 to their width (about 0.6s). While the vote is saving, the meta line says "Saving your vote…"

change.title: Change vote
change.html:
"People misclick. Let them change their vote."

  • A Change vote link in the results meta line (disabled while saving). It hides the results and makes the options clickable again ("Pick a new option" + Cancel).
  • Picking a different option moves the vote optimistically (−1 old, +1 new; total stays 101) and calls vote again. Picking the same option just returns to the results.

hints: Derived: const total = poll.options.reduce((sum, o) => { return sum + o.votes; }, 0); and const showResults = poll.myVote !== null;
Optimistic update without mutation: setPoll((prev) => { ... return { ...prev, myVote: optionId, options: prev.options.map((o) => { ... return { ...o, votes }; }) }; });
Animation: search mdn css transition width. A transition only runs if the same element changes width, so render the bar span in both states (width 0% before voting).
Can't vote twice: disabled={showResults || saving} on the option button.
Change: one boolean changing. showResults = poll.myVote !== null && !changing. In the optimistic update also subtract 1 from prev.myVote's option.
rubric: UI updates before the API resolves (optimistic)
Server response replaces the local guess
Total and percentages derived; percent() reused
Bars animate via a persistent element + CSS transition
No double voting (disabled while showing results / saving)
Change vote moves the count, total unchanged

dc34.title: Inline rename
dc34.summary: A deploy dashboard's project list. Double-click a name to edit it in place, Enter saves through the API, Escape cancels.
dc34.brief:
The Projects page of Deployd, a hosting dashboard. ProjectList loads projects with getProjects() and renders a ProjectRow each. Each row has an Edit button that does nothing.

Read api.ts: renameProject(id, name) takes 0.5–1s, returns the updated project, and throws if another project already has that name. StatusDot and formatAgo already exist.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next and Stretch. Change (~16 min): one row at a time.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–15 Core · 15–21 change · 21–25 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Editing needs a draft separate from the saved name so Escape can throw it away. I'll keep editingId, draft, error and saving in ProjectList, because the list owns projects and has to replace the renamed one. The row becomes presentational: it gets isEditing and callbacks. The input uses autoFocus and an onKeyDown for Enter and Escape. Save trims, rejects empty, calls the API, then maps the updated project into the list."
requirements: Double-clicking a project name, or clicking Edit, replaces the name with a focused input holding the current name (text selected). The actions become Cancel and Save
Enter (or Save) calls renameProject(id, name.trim()). While waiting the input is disabled and Save reads "Saving…". On success the row shows the new name and leaves edit mode
Escape (or Cancel) leaves edit mode and the old name is shown, with no API call
An empty (or whitespace-only) name is not saved: the input gets a red border and "Name can't be empty" appears under it; you stay in edit mode. Saving an unchanged name just closes the editor
If the API rejects (e.g. renaming "Docs" to "marketing site"), stay in edit mode and show the error message from the API under the input

change.title: Only one row at a time
change.html:
"QA opened three editors at once and lost track of which one they saved."

  • Only one row can be in edit mode. Starting to edit another row closes the first one (its draft is discarded).
  • While a save is in progress, the other rows' Edit buttons are disabled.

If you put isEditing state inside each row, this is where you lift it to the list as a single editingId.

hints: Keep a draft string separate from project.name. Copy the name into it when editing starts; Escape just leaves edit mode.
Keys: function handleKeyDown(e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) { if (e.key === "Enter") { onSave(); } if (e.key === "Escape") { onCancel(); } }. Search: mdn KeyboardEvent key.
Focus: the input only exists while editing, so autoFocus works. Select all with onFocus={(e) => { e.target.select(); }}.
Replace the saved project: setProjects((prev) => { return prev.map((p) => { if (p.id === updated.id) { return updated; } return p; }); });
Errors from the API: renameProject(id, name).then(...).catch((err: Error) => { setSaving(false); setError(err.message); });
Change: one editingId: string | null in the list; each row gets isEditing={p.id === editingId}. One id can only match one row.
rubric: Draft separate from saved value; Escape discards it
Enter/Escape handled on the input
Empty name blocked with a visible message
Saving state disables input and buttons
API error caught and shown; stays in edit mode
Single editingId in the list enforces one editor
List updated immutably with the server's project

dc35.title: School month calendar
dc35.summary: A school family portal. Replace the agenda list with a 7-column month grid with events, prev/next month, and a day panel.
dc35.brief:
The family portal of Maple Grove Elementary. SchoolCalendar gets a fixed today prop (Sept 15, 2026; never use Date.now) and shows this month's events from getEvents(year, month) as a flat list. The ‹ › buttons do nothing.

Read utils/date.ts: daysInMonth, firstWeekday, toKey, formatLongDate, WEEKDAYS, MONTH_NAMES. Months are 0-based like Date. EventChip renders one event. getEvents takes 0.4–0.9s.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~19 min): day side panel.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–19 Core · 19–26 change · 26–30 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The visible month is state, { year, month }, starting from today. The effect refetches when it changes, with the cancelled guard so a slow response for the old month can't land. The cells are derived: N blanks for the first weekday, then days 1..N, then blanks to fill the last row. Events are matched to cells by toKey. Prev/next use new Date(year, month ± 1, 1) so December → January rolls the year for me."
requirements: A 7-column grid with Sun–Sat headings. September 2026 starts on a Tuesday, so the 1st is in the third column; blank cells fill before the 1st and after the last day so every row has 7
Each day cell shows the day number and up to 2 EventChips for that date. If there are more, show "+1 more" (Sept 15 has 3 events). Today (the today prop) has a yellow circle on its number
‹ and › change the month (title "October 2026") and fetch that month's events. Going back from January goes to December of the previous year
While a month is loading, show a small "Loading…" next to the title. A slow response for a month you already left must not overwrite the current one
The agenda list is gone; the Legend stays under the grid

change.title: Day side panel
change.html:
"Parents need to see the times."

  • Clicking a day selects it (green outline) and opens a panel to the right of the grid titled with formatLongDate ("Tuesday, September 15") listing that day's events with their time, or "All day".
  • A day without events says "No events this day." A ✕ closes the panel. Changing month clears the selection.

hints: State: const [view, setView] = useState({ year: today.getFullYear(), month: today.getMonth() }); and use [view.year, view.month] as the effect dependencies.
Cells: const cells: (number | null)[] = []; push null firstWeekday(...) times, then 1..daysInMonth(...), then null while cells.length % 7 !== 0.
Month arithmetic: search mdn Date constructor month overflow. new Date(2026, 12, 1) is January 2027.
CSS: display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr));. The minmax(0, …) stops long chips from stretching a column.
Change: store selectedKey (the "YYYY-MM-DD" string), not a Date or the events. The panel's events are events.filter((e) => { return e.date === selectedKey; }).
rubric: Visible month in state, separate from today
Refetch effect keyed on year+month with cancelled guard
Cells derived (blanks + days + trailing blanks)
Year rollover handled by Date, not by hand
Reused date utils and EventChip
Selection stored as a key; panel derived from events
Grid uses CSS grid with minmax(0,1fr)

dc36.title: Chat: optimistic send
dc36.summary: A travel-concierge chat. Send messages optimistically with Sending… / Failed · Retry states, auto-scroll, and day separators.
dc36.brief:
The concierge chat of Wayfarer. ChatThread loads the conversation with getMessages() and renders MessageBubbles. The composer is a controlled input, but sending does nothing.

Read api.ts: sendMessage(text) takes 0.6–1.1s and returns the saved Message with a real id. To simulate a flaky network, a message containing "fail" throws the first time it's sent and succeeds on retry. utils/time.ts has formatTime, dayLabel and a fixed NOW_ISO.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~19 min): date separators.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–19 Core · 19–26 change · 26–30 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Each message in state gets a status: sent, sending or failed. On submit I append a message with a temporary id and status sending, clear the input, and call the API. Success swaps the temp message for the server's one (matched by temp id); failure flips its status to failed. Retry sets it back to sending and calls the same deliver function. Auto-scroll is an effect on messages.length that sets scrollTop = scrollHeight on a ref to the scroll container."
requirements: Submitting the composer (Enter or Send) adds your message to the bottom immediately, faded, with "Sending…" under it, and clears the input. Empty messages are ignored and Send is disabled while empty
When sendMessage resolves, the message becomes normal and shows its time ("3:01 PM")
If it throws, the bubble turns red and shows "Failed · Retry". Retry sets it back to "Sending…" and sends the same text again (it succeeds the second time)
The thread scrolls to the bottom after the first load and whenever a message is added

change.title: Date separators
change.html:
"It's hard to tell which day an answer came."

  • Before the first message of each day, show a centered pill separator with a line on both sides: Thu, Oct 8, Yesterday, Today (use dayLabel).
  • New messages sent today don't add another separator.

Hint: build the rows in a loop above the return, remembering the previous day label.

hints: Extend the type locally: type ChatMessage = Message & { status: "sent" | "sending" | "failed" }; and map the loaded messages to status: "sent".
Form submit: <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}> and e.preventDefault() first. Search: mdn preventDefault form submit.
Temp id: const tempId = "temp-" + Date.now(); Pass it to the API callback so you know which message to replace, even if two sends overlap.
Auto-scroll: useEffect(() => { const el = listRef.current; if (el) { el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight; } }, [messages.length]); Search: mdn scrollHeight.

Change: const rows: React.ReactNode[] = []; let lastDay = ""; messages.forEach((m) => { const day = dayLabel(m.sentAt); if (day !== lastDay) { rows.push(...); lastDay = day; } rows.push(<MessageBubble ... />); });
rubric: Optimistic insert with a temp id
Success replaces by temp id; failure flips status (no mutation)
Retry reuses the same send function
Scroll handled with a ref + effect, not on every render
Form submit with preventDefault; empty blocked
Separators computed while building rows, using dayLabel

notes: max-w 75% · pad 9 12 · radius 16 (4 on the tail corner)

dc37.title: City autocomplete
dc37.summary: A flight search "To" field. Suggestions from an API as you type, full keyboard and mouse support, match highlighting, and recent searches.
dc37.brief:
The search hero of skyhop. SearchPanel renders a CityInput for "To", which is just a controlled input right now.

Read api.ts: searchCities(query) takes 0.25–0.7s, so responses can arrive out of order while typing. getRecentSearches() takes 0.2–0.5s. utils/format.ts has formatCity ("Lisbon, Portugal").

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~23 min): recent searches.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–23 Core + Next · 23–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"All state lives in CityInput: query, results, loading, open, activeIndex. An effect on query calls the API with a cancelled flag, which also fixes out-of-order responses. activeIndex is the one thing both keyboard and mouse change; Enter picks results[activeIndex]. Selecting fills the input with formatCity and closes. Closing on blur would kill the click on an option, so options use onMouseDown + preventDefault."
requirements: Typing shows a dropdown under the field with up to 6 suggestions from searchCities: pin icon, "City, Country" and the airport code. While the first results load: "Searching…"; no matches: No cities match "xyz". Stale responses never overwrite newer ones
The typed part of each suggestion is highlighted (bold, primary color) with a <mark>, e.g. typing "lo" highlights "Lo" in "London" and "lo" in "Barcelona"
Clicking a suggestion fills the input with "City, Country", closes the dropdown and shows the code as a small badge next to the input
ArrowDown/ArrowUp move a highlighted row (wrapping around), Enter selects it (without submitting the form), Escape closes. Hovering a row highlights it too: there is only ever one highlighted row
Blurring the input closes the dropdown, but clicking a suggestion still works. The input has role="combobox", aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant

change.title: Recent searches
change.html:
"Most people fly to the same few places."

  • When the input is focused and empty, show a "Recent searches" heading and the cities from getRecentSearches() (clock icon instead of the pin).
  • Keyboard and mouse work on that list the same way. Selecting any city (from search or recents) moves it to the top of recents (no duplicates, max 5).

Hint: one derived options array (recents when the query is empty, otherwise results) means the keyboard code doesn't change at all.

hints: Effect: useEffect(() => { if (query.trim() === "") { setResults([]); return; } let cancelled = false; searchCities(query).then((data) => { if (cancelled) { return; } setResults(data); }); return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, [query]); The cleanup of the old query runs before the new one starts.
Highlight: search mdn String indexOf. Split the label into before / match / after with slice, and wrap the middle in <mark>.
Keys: e.preventDefault() on ArrowUp/Down (stops the caret jumping) and on Enter (stops the form submitting). Wrap with (prev + 1) % options.length.
Blur fires before click. Search: react onBlur before onClick dropdown. Fix: onMouseDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }} on each option keeps focus in the input.
Reset activeIndex to -1 whenever the query changes, otherwise it can point past the end of a shorter list.
Change: let options = results; if (query.trim() === "") { options = recent; } and update recents with [city, ...prev.filter(...)].slice(0, 5).
rubric: Out-of-order responses handled (cancelled flag in the effect)
Single activeIndex shared by keyboard and mouse
preventDefault on arrows and Enter
Blur/click race solved with mousedown preventDefault
Highlight without dangerouslySetInnerHTML
Basic combobox ARIA
Recents reuse the same options pipeline

dc38.title: File explorer tree
dc38.summary: An in-browser IDE. Build a recursive, expandable file tree, a preview pane that loads file contents, and a breadcrumb.
dc38.brief:
The editor of Codebox, a dark IDE. Explorer loads the nested tree with getTree() but only lists the top level; folders don't open. Preview just says "Select a file to preview it".

Read api.ts: folders have children; getFile(id) takes 0.3–0.8s. components/CodeView.tsx renders code with line numbers; utils/files.ts has fileIcon and formatBytes.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~23 min): Collapse all + file counts.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–23 Core + Next · 23–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"A TreeNode component renders one row and, if it's an open folder, maps its children to TreeNode again with depth + 1. Expanded folders are one Set of ids in Explorer, not state in each node, so they survive re-renders and can be cleared at once. The selected file is needed by both the explorer (highlight) and the preview (load), so it lives in App. Each node passes its path down, so on select I already have the breadcrumb."
requirements: Folders show a ▸ chevron (rotated ▾ when open) and toggle open/closed on click; files show their fileIcon badge. Children are indented 14px per level, to any depth (src/utils/api/client.ts is 3 levels deep). src starts open
Clicking a file highlights it (tinted row + purple left edge) and the preview loads it with getFile: "Loading…" then CodeView. Clicking another file quickly never shows the first file's content
The preview header shows a breadcrumb: codebox-web › src › components › Button.tsx (last part bold), and the size on the right with formatBytes
Collapsing a folder that contains the selected file keeps the file selected and previewed
The tree has role="tree", folders' items have aria-expanded

change.title: Collapse all + file counts
change.html:
"The tree gets long. Give me a reset, and tell me how big folders are."

  • A Collapse all button in the Explorer header closes every folder (disabled when nothing is open).
  • Each folder shows a small muted pill on the right with the number of files inside it, counting all nested folders (src shows 9).

If you kept open state inside each TreeNode, this is the moment you have to lift it.

hints: Recursive component: function TreeNode({ node, depth, ... }) { ... children = node.children.map((child) => { return <TreeNode key={child.id} node={child} depth={depth + 1} ... />; }) }. Search: react recursive component tree.
Indent with an inline style: style={{ paddingLeft: 10 + depth * 14 }}.
Set in state: never .add on the current set. setExpanded((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); ...; return next; }). Search: mdn Set.
Breadcrumb: pass parentPath down. Each node computes const path = [...parentPath, node.name]; and sends it up with onSelect({ id, path }).
Preview fetch: useEffect on the selected id with the cancelled guard, so a slow first file can't overwrite the second.
Change: function countFiles(node: FileNode): number { if (node.type === "file") { return 1; } ... sum countFiles(child) ... }. Collapse all is setExpanded(new Set()).
rubric: Recursive TreeNode with depth-based indent
Expanded state as one immutable Set at the top
Selection lifted to App (explorer + preview both need it)
Path built while recursing, not searched afterwards
File fetch guarded against stale responses
Recursive count as a pure function
Reused CodeView, fileIcon, formatBytes

dc39.title: Employee directory table
dc39.summary: An HR directory. Combine search, a department filter, sortable columns and pagination, then add column visibility toggles.
dc39.brief:
The Directory page of Peoplebase. EmployeeTable loads all 28 employees with getEmployees() (0.5–1.1s) and renders every one in a plain table.

Read components/: Pagination (Prev / "Page 2 of 4" / Next) and DeptBadge already exist. DEPARTMENTS is exported from api.ts. formatDate is in utils/format.ts.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~26 min): column toggles.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–7 plan out loud · 7–26 Core + Next · 26–35 change · 35–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The only state is the inputs: query, dept, sortKey, sortDir, page. Everything else is a pipeline computed on each render: filter by query, filter by department, copy and sort, then slice the page. Every handler that changes a filter also sets page back to 1, because page 3 of the old list might not exist. I'll describe the columns in one array so the header and cells are both maps over it, which also makes the sort buttons uniform."
requirements: A toolbar above the table: a search input ("Search name or title", case-insensitive on name OR title) and a department select ("All departments" + each department). Both apply together
Every column header is a button that sorts by it: first click ascending ▲, second descending ▼; other headers show a muted ↕. Default: Name ascending. Start date sorts by date
8 rows per page with the existing Pagination component, and "Showing 9–16 of 28" on the left of the footer. Changing the search, department or sort goes back to page 1

dc40.title: @mentions in comments
dc40.summary: An expense-approval thread. Typing "@" + letters in the comment box opens a filtered people dropdown that inserts "@Name ".
dc40.brief:
An expense report in Ledgerly. The right column shows the discussion (CommentList, which already highlights @First Last mentions) and a CommentBox textarea whose Comment button works.

Read api.ts: getUsers() takes 0.4–0.9s and returns the six people you can mention. components/Avatar.tsx takes a name and color.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~23 min): keyboard navigation.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–23 Core + Next · 23–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"CommentBox loads users on mount. On every change I look at the text before the caret (selectionStart): if it ends with @letters at the start or after a space, I store { start, query }, otherwise null. Suggestions are derived from that. Inserting replaces text.slice(start, start + 1 + query.length) with @Name . Because the value changes, React moves the caret to the end, so I put it back with setSelectionRange after the update."
requirements: Typing "@" followed by letters (at the start or after a space) opens a dropdown under the textarea with up to 5 people whose first or last name starts with those letters (case-insensitive): avatar, name, role. "@p" shows Priya Shah, Paula Reyes and Peter Nguyen; "@pa" only Paula
Clicking a person replaces the typed "@pa" with "@Paula Reyes " (with a trailing space) and closes the dropdown. Text before and after is kept
Pressing Enter while the dropdown is open inserts the first person instead of a newline
After inserting, focus stays in the textarea and the caret is right after the inserted name (also when inserting in the middle of the text)
The dropdown closes when the fragment no longer matches (e.g. you type a space), when nobody matches, and on blur. An email like "a@b" does not open it

change.title: Keyboard navigation
change.html:
"Our power users never touch the mouse."

  • ArrowDown/ArrowUp move a highlighted row in the dropdown (wrapping around); hovering highlights too.
  • Enter inserts the highlighted person, Escape closes the dropdown without changing the text. The highlight resets to the first row when the typed letters change.

hints: Caret position: search mdn HTMLTextAreaElement selectionStart. In onChange, e.target.selectionStart is where the caret is right after that keystroke.
Detect the fragment with a regex on the text before the caret: /(^|\s)@([a-zA-Z]*)$/.exec(value.slice(0, caret)). Group 2 is the query; start = caret - query.length - 1.
Insert: text.slice(0, start) + "@" + user.name + " " + text.slice(start + 1 + query.length).

Restoring the caret: the DOM value updates after the render, so wait one frame: requestAnimationFrame(() => { el.focus(); el.setSelectionRange(pos, pos); }); with a useRef on the textarea. Search: mdn setSelectionRange.
Clicking an option blurs the textarea first. Use onMouseDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }} on options so the click still lands.
Change: activeIndex state, reset to 0 in handleChange; in onKeyDown only act when the dropdown is open, and preventDefault for arrows, Enter and Escape.
rubric: Detection based on text before the caret, not the whole text
Mention state is {start, query}; suggestions derived
Correct splice keeps the surrounding text
Caret restored after the controlled value changes
Enter inserts instead of newline only while open
Blur/click race handled
Keyboard index wraps and resets on query change
